issue.title: Continuous memory leak
issue.body:
There is a memory leak in the parent process of Celery's worker.
It is not a child process executing a task.
It happens suddenly every few days.
Unless you stop Celery, it consumes server memory in tens of hours.

This problem happens at least in Celery 4.1, and it also occurs in Celery 4.2.
Celery is running on Ubuntu 16 and brokers use RabbitMQ.

![memory](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/280983/41805959-fcdd7700-76ed-11e8-9e02-db322818e924.jpeg)

issue.title: What is --statedb for?
issue.body:
# Checklist

- [x] I have checked the [issues list](https://github.com/celery/celery/issues?utf8=%E2%9C%93&q=is%3Aissue+label%3A%22Category%3A+Documentation%22+)
  for similar or identical bug reports.
- [x] I have checked the [pull requests list](https://github.com/celery/celery/pulls?q=is%3Apr+label%3A%22Category%3A+Documentation%22)
  for existing proposed fixes.
- [x] I have checked the [commit log](https://github.com/celery/celery/commits/main)
  to find out if the bug was already fixed in the main branch.
- [x] I have included all related issues and possible duplicate issues in this issue
      (If there are none, check this box anyway).

## Related Issues and Possible Duplicates

#### Related Issues

- The docs at https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/main/reference/celery.worker.state.html seem incomplete and maybe incorrect:
    ```
    Stores worker state between restarts.

    This is the persistent data stored by the worker when [celery worker --statedb](https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/main/reference/cli.html#cmdoption-celery-worker-S) is enabled.

    Currently only stores revoked task id’s.
    ```
    whereas the code make reference to active_requests, reserved_requests and revoked requests.

- #8069 points to internals documentation that says the worker stores et/countdown in a memory heapq. How does that relate to this?

#### Possible Duplicates

- None

# Description

I need to understand if/how tasks invoked with `apply_async()` using either `eta` or `countdown` are persisted or not, across celery restarts and broker restarts.

From tests of restarting celery, or invoking `apply_async(, ...countdown=n)`  it seems that on restarts, the task is found and run even though I am NOT using --statedb.

From the documentation of --statedb, I cannot tell if I should be using it or not in order to ensure `apply_async() works:

- Across celery restarts
- Across broker restarts

See also the related issues noted above. 

# Suggestions

I'd be happy to draft a PR updated docs once I know the facts. I'm think that  https://github.com/celery/celery/blob/main/docs/userguide/tasks.rst should have a section called something like "lifecycle of a task" with:

1. Client calls .apply/.appy_async
...
6. Message written to broker
...
9. Message read by worker
...
11. Message put in timerq
...
13. Task run
...
15. results written
...
17. Task acked to broker
